attribution: All descriptions paraphrase Carroll Quigley in The Anglo-American Establishment. Network-control assertions are author interpretations, not independently verified facts. PDF pages are exact 1-based file pages.

events.title: Hotel Majestic international-affairs meeting
events.description: Quigley describes British and American peace-conference experts meeting to plan an institute and history of the Peace Conference; Tasker Bliss chaired at Robert Cecil’s suggestion.

events.title: History of the Peace Conference published
events.description: Quigley describes six volumes edited by Harold Temperley, financed initially by Thomas Lamont’s £2,000 gift, appearing from 1920 through 1924.

events.title: Chatham House acquired for institute
events.description: Quigley describes Colonel R. W. Leonard buying the former Kinnaird house after Curtis interested him in the institute; an endowment commitment provoked an internal dispute.

events.title: Pacific Relations institute organized, in author’s account
events.description: Quigley describes a private Pacific Basin study organization founded at Atlantic City in September 1924. This is the book’s dating, not independent verification.

events.title: First listed IPR conference at Honolulu
events.description: Quigley describes the first of the listed international Pacific Relations conferences, followed by Honolulu in 1927 and Kyoto in 1929.

events.title: Stevenson endowment supports Survey and chair
events.description: Quigley describes Daniel Stevenson’s £20,000 endowment financing the international-affairs Survey and a London research chair held by Arnold Toynbee.

events.title: Intellectual Cooperation institute transferred to League
events.description: Quigley describes the French government establishing the institute and handing it to the League; Alfred Zimmern served as deputy director from 1926 to 1930.

events.title: Institute journal opens to public subscription
events.description: Quigley describes the journal becoming available to public subscribers rather than members alone; it later took the name International Affairs.

events.title: Canadian and Australian institutes formed
events.description: Quigley describes the earliest Dominion international-affairs institutes being created around local Round Table circles.

events.title: Pacific Council organized
events.description: Quigley describes a continuing central council formed between IPR meetings.

events.title: Abe Bailey promises perpetual annual funding
events.description: Quigley describes Bailey pledging £5,000 annually to the institute, conditioned on its membership being limited to British subjects.

events.title: International Studies Conferences begin in Berlin
events.description: Quigley describes Zimmern initiating annual international round-table meetings under the intellectual-cooperation institute.

events.title: RIIA acquires Wheeler-Bennett information services
events.description: Quigley describes the institute paying £3,500 for John Wheeler-Bennett’s information services and making them its Information Department.

events.title: Rockefeller funds RIIA study groups
events.description: Quigley describes a grant of £8,000 a year for five years to develop study-group research, renewed for another five years in 1937.

events.title: Toronto Commonwealth relations conference
events.description: Quigley describes the first unofficial conference deciding to extend institutes to New Zealand, South Africa, India, and Newfoundland.

events.title: Chatham House collective-security conference
events.description: Quigley describes 39 delegates from 14 countries assembling to discuss collective security; Meston presided and Allen Dulles chaired study meetings.

events.title: Indian Institute of International Affairs established
events.description: Quigley describes the Indian institute being established at a meeting convened at the Viceroy’s house by Willingdon.

events.title: Curtis and Macadam visit international institutes
events.description: Quigley describes Curtis and Macadam touring Australia, New Zealand and Canada and attending the Princeton Pacific Council meeting before separate American institutional visits.

events.title: RIIA refugee study published
events.description: Quigley describes a refugee research program begun in 1937 producing a report edited by John Hope Simpson, whom Quigley explicitly distinguishes from the Group.

events.title: Foreign Research and Press Service formed
events.description: Quigley describes Chatham House research resources moving to Oxford after war began, supporting government departments under Toynbee and Curtis.

events.title: Foreign Office takes over FRPS
events.description: Quigley describes FRPS merging with the Political Intelligence Department to form a Research Department, directed by Toynbee with Zimmern as deputy.

events.title: Curtis forms India constitutional study group
events.description: Quigley describes Curtis forming an unofficial London Round Table study circle on introducing responsible government to India; exact original membership is explicitly uncertain.

events.title: Montagu announces responsible-government policy
events.description: Quigley describes Montagu announcing gradual development of responsible government in India, followed by the Montagu–Chelmsford Report.

events.title: Government of India Act introduces dyarchy
events.description: Quigley describes constitutional reform developed from the Montagu–Chelmsford proposals and amended by Selborne’s committee; Quigley stresses an unofficial Curtis circle in its intellectual background.

events.title: Irwin announces Dominion-status goal and conference
events.description: Quigley describes the Viceroy announcing a Dominion-status goal and a Round Table Conference, provoking opposition in Britain.

events.title: First Indian Round Table Conference
events.description: Quigley describes delegations from Britain, British India and the Indian States considering federation; Gandhi’s party did not participate.

events.title: Second Indian Round Table Conference
events.description: Quigley describes a second conference with broadly similar delegations and additional members; Rushbrook Williams represented Nawanagar.

events.title: Third Indian Round Table Conference
events.description: Quigley describes the third session without Labour representatives and with Hoare, Simon, Lothian and Halifax among the British delegates.

events.title: Hoare introduces Government of India Bill
events.description: Quigley describes Hoare introducing the bill in the Commons, with Churchill leading strong opposition.

events.title: Halifax meets Hitler at Berchtesgaden
events.description: Quigley describes Halifax’s conversation with Hitler concerning European changes and a possible four-power understanding; Quigley analyzes the German memorandum and differing interpretations.

events.title: Halifax replaces Eden as Foreign Secretary
events.description: Quigley describes Halifax replacing Eden after disagreements over recognition of Italy’s conquest of Ethiopia.

events.title: Lothian becomes ambassador to United States
events.description: Quigley describes Lothian’s appointment as ambassador and the importance Quigley assigns to his American and Rhodes Scholarship connections.

events.title: Lothian dies; Halifax chosen for Washington
events.description: Quigley describes Lothian’s death leading to Halifax moving from the Foreign Office to the Washington ambassadorship while retaining War Cabinet status.

events.title: Brand begins wartime American service
events.description: Quigley describes Brand working in America through May 1946, first heading the British Food Mission and later representing the Treasury.

events.title: Isaiah Berlin joins Washington embassy
events.description: Quigley describes Berlin becoming First Secretary after working with Wheeler-Bennett in the Ministry of Information’s New York branch.

events.title: Agenda journal founded for reconstruction
events.description: Quigley describes a quarterly reconstruction journal established at the end of 1942 under LSE auspices, edited by G. N. Clark with offices at Chatham House.

events.title: Arthur Salter moves from shipping mission to UNRRA
events.description: Quigley describes Salter joining UNRRA as Senior Deputy Director General when the organization was established in the author’s account.

events.title: Labour victory alters postwar network influence
events.description: Quigley describes the Labour government’s arrival disrupting the Group’s reconstruction influence; Quigley’s month is inconsistent with standard election chronology, so the event retains year precision.

events.title: Britain rejects Geneva Protocol
events.description: Quigley describes Austen Chamberlain rejecting the protocol at the League Council, while Dove, Curtis, Kerr and Wilson Harris visited Geneva; Quigley treats rejection as a setback to collective security.

events.title: Locarno agreements reshape European guarantees
events.description: Quigley describes the guarantees involving Germany, France, Belgium, Britain and Italy; he argues their legal structure weakened French support for eastern allies. The critical assessment is the author’s interpretation.

events.title: Anglo-German Naval Agreement
events.description: Quigley describes Britain accepting a German navy up to 35 percent of British fleet size and up to parity in submarines; he condemns the effect on French strategic security.

events.title: Germany remilitarizes Rhineland
events.description: Quigley describes German remilitarization and Britain’s response, which he regards as a crucial appeasement turning point; Halifax accompanied Eden to the ensuing Paris discussions.

events.title: Munich crisis and Czechoslovak settlement
events.description: Quigley describes Chamberlain’s September negotiations with Hitler and the settlement yielding Czechoslovak territory; he interprets British crisis publicity and diplomatic pressure as deliberate efforts to secure acquiescence.

events.title: German occupation of Bohemia and Moravia
events.description: Quigley describes the occupation prompting a turn in the Group’s publicly expressed policy toward a grand alliance, which he contrasts with continued private appeasement by Chamberlain’s circle.

events.title: Britain guarantees Polish independence
events.description: Quigley describes Chamberlain’s unilateral guarantee, noting the distinction between independence and territorial integrity and criticizing the absence of immediate military implementation.

events.title: National Service Act follows conscription campaign
events.description: Quigley describes the legislation resulting from a preparedness campaign associated with Amery, Grigg, Lothian and The Times.

organizations.name: Royal Institute of International Affairs (Chatham House)
organizations.description: Quigley describes an international-affairs discussion, study and publication institute; he attributes decisive founding initiative and influence to Curtis and the Milner circle.

organizations.name: Institute of Pacific Relations
organizations.description: Quigley describes a private organization studying Pacific Basin affairs through national units, conferences and a Pacific Council.

organizations.name: Pacific Council of the IPR
organizations.description: Quigley describes the continuing self-perpetuating central IPR body established in 1927.

organizations.name: Canadian Institute of International Affairs
organizations.description: Quigley describes a Dominion institute founded in 1927 around Round Table participants.

organizations.name: Australian Institute of International Affairs
organizations.description: Quigley describes a Dominion institute with Eggleston among its founders and Thomas Bavin as president in 1934–1941.

organizations.name: New Zealand Institute of International Affairs
organizations.description: Quigley describes a Dominion institute headed by Downie Stewart from 1935 onward.

organizations.name: South African Institute of International Affairs
organizations.description: Quigley describes a Dominion institute in which B. K. Long was an important participant.

organizations.name: Indian Institute of International Affairs
organizations.description: Quigley describes an institute set up in 1936 at Willingdon’s convened meeting.

organizations.name: Council on Foreign Relations
organizations.description: Quigley describes a New York international-affairs organization closely related to Chatham House; his account attributes influence to Morgan-connected American experts.

organizations.name: International Institute of Intellectual Cooperation
organizations.description: Quigley describes a Paris executive institute handed to the League by France in 1926.

organizations.name: International Committee on Intellectual Cooperation
organizations.description: Quigley describes an international advisory committee connected to the League, chaired by Murray from 1928 to 1945.

organizations.name: International Studies Conferences
organizations.description: Quigley describes a network of national coordinating committees and international organizations assembling for thematic discussion.

organizations.name: Rockefeller Foundation
organizations.description: Quigley describes a philanthropic foundation granting money to RIIA study groups; Greene was trustee and secretary in 1913–1917.

organizations.name: Foreign Research and Press Service
organizations.description: Quigley describes a wartime Oxford research service answering government questions, reviewing foreign press and preparing studies.

organizations.name: Foreign Office Research Department
organizations.description: Quigley describes the government research department resulting from the April 1943 FRPS merger.

organizations.name: Indian Round Table Conferences
organizations.description: Quigley describes three constitutional reform conferences bringing British, British Indian and princely-state delegates together.

organizations.name: India Office
organizations.description: Quigley describes the British department overseeing Indian affairs and constitutional reform.

organizations.name: British Embassy in Washington
organizations.description: Quigley describes a wartime diplomatic center for British-American relations, staffed by numerous people Quigley connects to All Souls and the Milner circle.

organizations.name: British Food Mission
organizations.description: Quigley describes a British wartime mission in America headed for three years by Brand.

organizations.name: British Merchant Shipping Mission
organizations.description: Quigley describes a wartime American mission headed by Salter from 1941 until his move to UNRRA.

organizations.name: United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration
organizations.description: Quigley describes an international relief organization employing Salter as a senior deputy director general.

organizations.name: Ministry of Information
organizations.description: Quigley describes a British wartime information ministry whose personnel Quigley associates with his network.

organizations.name: Ministry of Production
organizations.description: Quigley describes a British wartime economic mobilization ministry headed by Oliver Lyttelton in 1942–1945.

organizations.name: Ministry of Economic Warfare
organizations.description: Quigley describes an economic warfare ministry headed by Selborne in 1942–1945.

organizations.name: Agenda
organizations.description: Quigley describes a quarterly journal on postwar reconstruction with editorial offices at Chatham House.

people.name: G. M. Gathorne-Hardy
people.description: Quigley describes an honorary secretary of RIIA and its first journal editor.

people.name: Arnold J. Toynbee
people.description: Quigley describes the Survey editor and international-history professor who directed FRPS and the Foreign Office research organization.

people.name: Sir Neill Malcolm
people.description: Quigley describes RIIA council chairman in 1926–1935 and High Commissioner for German Refugees in 1936–1938.

people.name: Jerome D. Greene
people.description: Quigley describes a banker and foundation trustee who chaired the Pacific Council in 1929–1932.

people.name: Frederic W. Eggleston
people.description: Quigley describes an Australian institute founder, IPR conference leader and Australian minister in Washington in 1944–1946.

people.name: Ivison S. Macadam
people.description: Quigley describes Chatham House secretary from 1929 who traveled with Curtis to overseas institutes in 1938.

people.name: James Meston, Lord Meston
people.description: Quigley describes RIIA chairman in 1920–1926, a conference president, and a director involved in cement firms.

people.name: Waldorf Astor, Lord Astor
people.description: Quigley describes RIIA chairman from 1935 and a significant wartime benefactor.

people.name: John W. Wheeler-Bennett
people.description: Quigley describes an information-services founder, RIIA officer and British information worker in wartime New York.

people.name: Sir Alfred Zimmern
people.description: Quigley describes an intellectual-cooperation administrator, conference organizer and Foreign Office research deputy.

people.name: Gilbert Murray
people.description: Quigley describes a founder and chairman of the League’s intellectual-cooperation committee.

people.name: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
people.description: Quigley describes the Indian representative on the intellectual-cooperation committee in 1931–1939 and an Oxford professor and All Souls fellow.

people.name: Edwin S. Montagu
people.description: Quigley describes Secretary of State for India in 1917–1922 and co-author with Chelmsford of constitutional reform proposals.

people.name: Lord Chelmsford
people.description: Quigley describes Viceroy in 1916–1921 and collaborator in the Montagu–Chelmsford reforms.

people.name: Sir Samuel Hoare
people.description: Quigley describes Secretary of State for India in 1931–1935 and principal parliamentary advocate of the Government of India Act.

people.name: Malcolm Hailey, Lord Hailey
people.description: Quigley describes an Indian administrator and Hoare’s key adviser while the constitutional bill proceeded.

people.name: L. F. Rushbrook Williams
people.description: Quigley describes an adviser and delegate for Indian princes, later a BBC Eastern Service director and Times editor.

people.name: Sir John Simon
people.description: Quigley describes chair of the Indian Statutory Commission and participant in constitutional reform conferences.

people.name: Lord Willingdon
people.description: Quigley describes Viceroy in 1931–1936 who convened the founding meeting of the Indian international-affairs institute.

people.name: Edward Wood, Lord Halifax
people.description: Quigley describes Viceroy as Lord Irwin, later Foreign Secretary and wartime ambassador in Washington.

people.name: Adam D. Marris
people.description: Quigley describes Brand’s protégé, Lazard employee and wartime British diplomat in Washington.

people.name: Isaiah Berlin
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow who worked in British information services in New York before joining the Washington embassy.

people.name: Sir Arthur Salter
people.description: Quigley describes head of the British Merchant Shipping Mission and later a senior UNRRA official.

people.name: Roger Mellor Makins
people.description: Quigley describes a diplomat involved in refugee bodies, wartime Mediterranean administration and the Washington embassy.

people.name: H. V. Hodson
people.description: Quigley describes an RIIA economic writer and wartime official in information, Indian reform and production.

people.name: Cyril John Radcliffe
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow and wartime Director General of the Ministry of Information.

people.name: G. N. Clark
people.description: Quigley describes a historian and Agenda editor whom Quigley calls close to the Group but not a member.

people.name: Douglas P. T. Jay
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow and wartime economic administrator who became Attlee’s assistant and a Labour MP.

people.name: Percy E. Corbett
people.description: Quigley describes a Canadian academic, Pacific Council chairman in 1942 and wartime British Embassy lobbying participant.

people.name: General Tasker Bliss
people.description: Quigley describes the American delegate who chaired the Hotel Majestic meeting on 30 May 1919 at Robert Cecil’s suggestion.

people.name: Harold Temperley
people.description: Quigley describes a British participant at Hotel Majestic selected to edit the six-volume History of the Peace Conference.

people.name: Thomas W. Lamont
people.description: Quigley describes a J. P. Morgan associate whose £2,000 gift financed the committee preparing a history of the Peace Conference.

people.name: Colonel R. W. Leonard
people.description: Quigley describes a Canadian donor who bought the house at 10 St James Square for the institute in 1923, conditional on an upkeep endowment.

people.name: Sir Daniel Stevenson
people.description: Quigley describes the donor of the 1925 endowment financing the Survey and London research chair.

people.name: Sir Robert L. Borden
people.description: Quigley describes the first president of the Canadian international-affairs institute, serving in 1927–1931.

people.name: Allen W. Dulles
people.description: Quigley describes a Council on Foreign Relations participant who chaired study meetings and gave opening and closing speeches at the 1935 collective-security conference.

people.name: Sir Maurice Gwyer
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls member who joined the council of the Indian Institute of International Affairs at its establishment in 1936.

people.name: Sir John Hope Simpson
people.description: Quigley describes the editor of the institute’s 1939 refugee report; Quigley explicitly states he was not a member of the Group.

people.name: Anthony Eden
people.description: Quigley describes Foreign Secretary who communicated the FRPS takeover to Astor and later differed from Halifax and Chamberlain over foreign policy.

people.name: Sir William Duke
people.description: Quigley describes a former Bengal governor, member of Curtis’s study circle from 1914 and India Office Permanent Under Secretary in 1920–1924.

people.name: Sir Malcolm Seton
people.description: Quigley describes an India Office official joining Curtis’s study circle around 1913, subsequently Assistant and Deputy Under Secretary.

people.name: Mohandas Gandhi
people.description: Quigley describes the Indian nationalist leader whose party declined the first Round Table Conference on the terms offered.

people.name: Winston Churchill
people.description: Quigley describes a leading parliamentary opponent of Indian constitutional reform and critic of government armament policy and appeasement.

people.name: Adolf Hitler
people.description: Quigley describes Germany’s leader whose diplomatic and military actions are central to the chapter’s criticism of appeasement.

people.name: Neville Chamberlain
people.description: Quigley describes the British prime minister conducting negotiations with Hitler and issuing the 1939 Polish guarantee; Quigley distinguishes his policy circle from the Milner circle.

people.name: John Galway Foster
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow and private international law lecturer who served as First Secretary in Washington from 1939 and became a Conservative MP in 1945.

people.name: Robert J. Stopford
people.description: Quigley describes an RIIA reparations writer, technical adviser to the Runciman mission and financial counselor to the Washington embassy in 1940–1943.

people.name: Oliver Lyttelton
people.description: Quigley describes an industrial executive, President of the Board of Trade in 1940–1941 and Minister of Production in 1942–1945.

people.name: Lord Wolmer, third Earl of Selborne
people.description: Quigley describes the former Lord Wolmer, director of cement regulation in 1940–1942 and Minister of Economic Warfare in 1942–1945.

people.name: Charles R. S. Harris
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow, former Times writer and Brand associate serving in economic warfare, diplomatic and military posts during the war.

people.name: Clement Attlee
people.description: Quigley describes a Labour critic of the India bill who became prime minister of the postwar Labour government.

people.name: N. W. Rowell
people.description: Quigley describes the second president of the Canadian international-affairs institute and a member of the Pacific Council in 1930.

people.name: Sir James Allen
people.description: Quigley describes New Zealand’s member of the Pacific Council in the 1930 membership list.

people.name: I. Nitobe
people.description: Quigley describes Japan’s member of the Pacific Council in the 1930 membership list.

people.name: D. Z. T. Yui
people.description: Quigley describes China’s member of the Pacific Council in the 1930 membership list.

people.name: Sir Thomas Bavin
people.description: Quigley describes president of the Australian international-affairs institute in 1934–1941.

people.name: W. Downie Stewart
people.description: Quigley describes president of the New Zealand international-affairs institute from 1935.

people.name: B. K. Long
people.description: Quigley describes a former member of Milner’s Kindergarten active in the South African international-affairs institute.

people.name: Vincent Massey
people.description: Quigley describes a vice-president of the Canadian international-affairs institute and one of the principal Canadian participants in Quigley’s network account.

people.name: Edward Grigg
people.description: Quigley describes Parliamentary Secretary to the wartime Ministry of Information until the 1940 cabinet revision, then serving in the War Office.

people.name: John H. A. Sparrow
people.description: Quigley describes an All Souls fellow on a confidential military mission in Washington in 1940 and attached to the War Office from 1942.

people.name: Leopold Amery
people.description: Quigley describes Secretary of State for India in 1940–1945, an opponent of coercive League policy before the war and advocate of conscription in 1939.

people.name: Sir Abe Bailey
people.description: Quigley describes a major RIIA founding benefactor whose gifts included £5,000 annually in perpetuity from 1928.

people.name: Sir Lionel Abrahams
people.description: Quigley describes an India Office Assistant Under Secretary who participated in Curtis’s constitutional study circle.

people.name: Sir Joseph Flavelle
people.description: Quigley describes a vice-president of the Canadian international-affairs institute and associate of the network in the First World War.

people.name: George Parkin Glazebrook
people.description: Quigley describes honorary secretary of the Canadian international-affairs institute and one of the principal Canadian network members in Quigley’s account.

people.name: Sir Henry Price
people.description: Quigley describes a donor who endowed a Chatham House economics chair in 1936 and gave £50,000 for library expansion in 1942.

people.name: Sir Harold Butler
people.description: Quigley describes a wartime minister in Washington from 1942 whose work chiefly concerned public relations.

people.name: Sir William Marris
people.description: Quigley describes Curtis’s associate in the development of Indian responsible-government ideas and father of Adam Marris.

people.name: Sir Cecil Hurst
people.description: Quigley describes a participant in planning the international-affairs institute and the legal drafter to whom Quigley attributes the structure of the Locarno agreements.

relationships.label: founding initiative
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Curtis provided the decisive initiative; Robert Cecil chaired the organizing committee.

relationships.label: funding
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Bailey supplied founding money and later a perpetual annual grant.

relationships.label: research and publications
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Toynbee edited the Survey and led wartime research.

relationships.label: institutional cooperation
relationships.description: According to Quigley, the institutes exchanged publications, books and personnel contacts; the branch characterization belongs to the author’s cited account.

relationships.label: governing body
relationships.description: According to Quigley, the Pacific Council supplied continuing central organization between meetings.

relationships.label: chairmanship
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Murray chaired the committee from 1928 to 1945.

relationships.label: deputy directorship
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Zimmern was deputy director from 1926 to 1930.

relationships.label: wartime research service
relationships.description: According to Quigley, library, information and press resources formed the FRPS.

relationships.label: merged into
relationships.description: According to Quigley, FRPS was absorbed with the Political Intelligence Department in April 1943.

relationships.label: policy advice
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Hailey was continuously available as Hoare’s principal adviser on the India bill.

relationships.label: delegate and adviser
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Williams advised the states delegation and then represented Nawanagar.

relationships.label: India constitutional study
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Curtis convened an unofficial circle whose original membership the author says is uncertain.

relationships.label: diplomatic meeting
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Halifax met Hitler on 19 November 1937; the policy interpretation is Quigley’s.

relationships.label: mentorship
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Marris was Brand’s protégé and a Lazard colleague.

relationships.label: family
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Adam was the son of William Marris.

relationships.label: wartime information work
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Berlin worked with Wheeler-Bennett in New York in 1941.

relationships.label: senior official
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Salter joined as Senior Deputy Director General.

relationships.label: director general
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Radcliffe led the ministry for more than four wartime years.

relationships.label: administrative leadership
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Hodson became principal assistant secretary and head of its Non-Munitions Division.

relationships.label: editorship
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Clark edited the reconstruction quarterly.

relationships.label: personal assistant
relationships.description: According to Quigley, Jay served as the prime minister’s personal assistant after Labour entered government.

notes: Quigley dates founding of IPR to September 1924 (PDF 193); preserve attribution rather than present as verified founding date.
PDF 306 dates Labour electoral victory to August 1945; use year precision and note source chronology discrepancy, rather than an independently corrected day.
Printed numbering does not stay a constant offset from PDF pages; citations should use PDF page numbers.
